title: Packaging and packaging waste consultation: minimum recycled plastic content
summary: Three opportunities to comment on future EU rules on minimum recycled content for plastic packaging
update:
The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation 2025/40 (PPWR) sets minimum recycled-content targets by 2030 for plastic packaging, including imported packaged food products, put on the European Union (EU) market. The EU will develop detailed rules to support these targets.

The European Commission has launched a series of consultations to gather technical and practical information, including information relevant to non-EU countries, to help it develop rules that reflect the current technologies, markets, and control systems for recycled plastics.

Interested stakeholders can provide feedback and evidence on:

Sustainability criteria for plastic recycling technologies Harmonisation of rules for calculating and verifying recycled content in plastic packaging . Conditions for importing recycled materials into the EU for use in packaging .
what_changing:
Under the PPWR (Regulation 2025/40 , Art. 7), plastic packaging, including imported packaged food products, put on the EU market from 2030 will have to meet minimum recycled-content targets.

The European Commission has launched three consultations to collect technical and practical evidence from stakeholders, including those based outside the EU, to help prepare the detailed rules that will support the implementation of these targets.

Interested stakeholders can provide feedback and evidence on the following.
why: To implement the recycled plastic content targets, the European Commission wants to develop rules that are workable, verifiable, and enforceable by collecting insights from operators.
timeline: The rules are expected to be adopted in the fourth quarter of 2026.
actions:
All interested stakeholders are invited to give feedback via the relevant European Commission Have Your Say platform until 16 September 2026 :

Sustainability criteria for plastic recycling technologies Harmonisation of rules for calculating and verifying recycled content in plastic packaging Conditions for importing recycled materials into the EU for use in packaging .

Stakeholders wishing to respond must be registered. Those who do not already have an account will first need to Create an EU login account , then register their organisation on the EU Transparency register .
background:
The PPWR requires plastic packaging to contain at least a minimum percentage of recycled plastic per unit of packaging by 2030, with more ambitious targets set for 2040. By 31 December 2026, the European Commission will indicate a methodology to calculate the amount of recycled content. For more details see New EU packaging rules explained .

Packaging is one of the main users of virgin materials and is a significant contributor to waste. In the EU, the share of recycled packaging has been growing slowly between 2014 and 2023 ( European Commission 2025 ) – but much recyclable packaging is still not recycled. This is because there are not enough suitable and economically viable collection and recycling processes.

The PPWR is part of the EU’s circular economy action plan ( European Commission 2020 ) which commits to making all packaging reusable or recyclable by 2030, and to reducing (over) packaging and packaging waste. To achieve this objective, the PPWR introduces minimum recycled-content targets for plastic packaging to reduce the use of primary raw materials and create demand for recycled plastics.
